content.title: About
content.content: Sour full‑fat cream is a dairy product obtained from cow’s milk cream with about 30 % fat. It has a characteristic tangy taste, a thick creamy texture and is widely used in sauces, desserts and baking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sour cream is produced by natural fermentation, where bacteria convert lactose into lactic acid.
In Russia sour cream is a traditional topping for borscht, okroshka and pancakes.
Full‑fat cream retains a richer flavor compared with low‑fat versions.
In some countries sour cream is called “smetana”, although smetana usually has a milder acidity.
Different bacterial cultures can be used, influencing aroma and texture.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Cream provides vitamin B2 (riboflavin) and vitamin B12, which support energy metabolism and the nervous system.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: While the fat is mainly saturated, monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids are also present and can benefit skin health.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Sour cream is a good source of calcium and phosphorus, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Probiotic bacteria
items.content: The fermentation cultures may have a positive effect on gut microbiota.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: Cream contains small amounts of vitamin D, which aids calcium absorption.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cream contains lactose, so people with intolerance should limit consumption.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because of its high fat, cream is calorie‑dense; moderation is important for weight management.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some individuals may react to casein or whey proteins.

items.title: Shelf life
items.content: Improper storage can lead to spoilage and growth of harmful bacteria.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sour cream is used in sauces (e.g., a classic sour‑cream sauce), casseroles, pancake batter, marinades and as a salad dressing. It can be stirred into soups at the end of cooking to add creaminess.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cream refrigerated at 0–4 °C in its original container or a sealed jar. After opening, use within 5–7 days. Freezing may alter texture, so frozen cream is best used in cooked dishes after thawing.
